speaker: Doctor
text:
What is the specific location of your knee pain, and did it happen suddenly or develop gradually after your increased activity?

I will also need to know if you experienced any swelling, redness, or a popping sound at the time of injury.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Did you hear a distinct "pop" or snapping sensation when the pain began, and is the pain localized more to the inner or outer side of the knee? Also, have you noticed any significant swelling or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome (MPFPS)
